description: The 'memo' hashtable in compute-depth is created but never used to cache results, leading to redundant work and potential performance issues on deep graphs, though the primary logic bug is the missed optimization and lack of use of the allocated resource.
suggested_fix: Store and look up results in the 'memo' hashtable before recursing into children.

description: Cycle detection in compute-depth uses only the first 8 bytes of the hash to check for visited blocks. This can lead to false positives (collisions) where valid branches are skipped because they share a prefix with a visited block.
suggested_fix: Use the full bytevector hash as the key in the visited list or set instead of truncating it to an integer.

description: scheme-eval-and-capture only parameterizes current-output-port. Output written to current-error-port (stderr) during evaluation will not be captured in the response sent back to the user.
suggested_fix: Parameterize both current-output-port and current-error-port to the same output-port.

description: utf8->string is called on raw block payloads without checking if they are valid UTF-8. Binary payloads will cause a crash during search operations.
suggested_fix: Wrap utf8->string in a guard to handle encoding errors or use a bytevector search function.

description: load-session-file uses cdr on the result of assq without checking if the key was found. This will crash if a session file is missing expected keys like 'tier', 'name', or 'model'.
suggested_fix: Check the result of assq before calling cdr, or use a helper that handles missing keys gracefully.

description: The implementation of get-identity-history returns the history in oldest-to-newest order (consing to a list and returning the leaf version first), which contradicts the docstring stating it returns 'newest first'.
code_snippet: (let loop ([hash head-hash] [acc '()]) (let ([block (fetch hash)]) (if (not block) acc ... (loop (vector-ref refs 0) new-acc))))
suggested_fix: Either update the comment to reflect the reality or reverse the resulting list if newest-first is truly desired.

description: The loop condition (>= (+ i 3) len) causes indexing to stop prematurely. For a payload of length 3, nothing is indexed. It should process the last 3 characters.
suggested_fix: Change the termination condition to (> (+ i 3) len).

description: find-blocks-by-content only uses the first 3 characters of the query string to look up blocks, effectively ignoring the rest of the query and potentially returning many false positives.
suggested_fix: Iterate through all 3-char fragments of the query and find the intersection of the results.

description: query-blocks maps fetch over all hashes and then passes the results to predicates. If a block is missing (fetch returns #f), predicates like tag-is will crash when calling block-tag on #f.
suggested_fix: Filter out #f results from the fetch step or ensure patterns handle #f inputs.

description: terminate-worker! sends SIGKILL immediately after SIGTERM if the process is still 'alive' according to process-alive?. Since process-alive? (kill -0) returns true as long as the process exists (even during shutdown), the worker never gets a chance to clean up gracefully.
suggested_fix: Add a small delay or loop to check for process exit before escalating to SIGKILL.
